exposure: Particulate matter with aerodynamic diameter <10 mm (PM10)
cohort: The study included 979,306 singleton live births for PTB analysis and 888,133 for TLBW analysis in Sao Paulo municipality between 2011 and 2016.
finding: Air pollution exposure (O3, PM10) was associated with increased chances of preterm birth and term low birth weight, and these associations were modified by maternal education and area-level socioeconomic status, indicating greater susceptibility for mothers with lower SES.
birth_weight: Term low birth weight was defined as weight < 2500 g on term deliveries.
gest_age: Preterm birth was defined as gestational age <37 weeks.
